documents.title: QA Lab Test Report – PH-200 Safety Evaluation
documents.content:
**QA LAB TEST REPORT – PH-200 SAFETY EVALUATION**

**Report No:** QA/TR/2024/118
**Date of Issue:** 12 March 2024
**Product:** Portable Heater Model PH-200
**Batch/Serial Range:** PH2-2401-001 through PH2-2401-450
**Test Date(s):** 5–8 March 2024
**Test Location:** QA Laboratory, Building 4, 17 Kembla Street, Wollongong NSW
**Test Engineer:** M. Okafor
**Reviewed By:** L. Tran, Senior QA Engineer

---

**1. OBJECTIVE**

To evaluate the safety performance of the Portable Heater Model PH-200 against the requirements of AS/NZS 60335.2.30:2023 (Household and similar electrical appliances – Safety – Particular requirements for room heaters) and internal specification QA-SP-114 Rev 4.

---

**2. SUMMARY OF FINDINGS**

The QA Lab report gives the Portable Heater Model PH-200 a safety_rating of 1 star. Record status: current. This rating is current as of the date of issue and supersedes the provisional rating assigned in Report QA/TR/2024/102.

| Test Category | Result | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| Thermal cut-out operation | **FAIL** | See Section 5.2 |
| Surface temperature rise | **FAIL** | Exceeds limit at multiple points |
| Stability / tip-over switch | **PASS** | Operated correctly in all orientations |
| Input power & current | **PASS** | Within tolerance |
| Supply cord anchorage | **PASS** | Withstood 100 N pull for 1 min |
| Protection against moisture | **PASS** | IPX1 spray test, no ingress |
| Abnormal operation (blocked outlet) | **FAIL** | Glow observed; see Section 5.4 |

Overall assessment: **NOT APPROVED** for sale or continued distribution. Refer to Section 7 for recommended actions.

---

**3. TEST CONDITIONS**

Ambient laboratory conditions were recorded at the start of each test session and are noted below. Conditions were within the required range for all tests unless otherwise stated.

| Date | Time | Temp (°C) | RH (%) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 05 Mar 2024 | 09:15 | 22.4 | 58 | Calibration check performed prior to start |
| 06 Mar 2024 | 10:05 | 23.1 | 55 | – |
| 07 Mar 2024 | 14:20 | 22.8 | 61 | Power fluctuation noted; UPS engaged |
| 08 Mar 2024 | 09:40 | 22.0 | 57 | – |

---

**4. EQUIPMENT AND CALIBRATION**

All measuring instruments were within their calibration validity period. Calibration certificates are on file.

| Equipment ID | Description | Cal Due Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| EQ-TC-07 | Thermocouple data logger, 16-ch | 15 Apr 2024 | Valid |
| EQ-PM-12 | Power analyser, 230 V / 10 A | 02 Jun 2024 | Valid |
| EQ-DMM-04 | Digital multimeter, true RMS | 20 Mar 2024 | Valid |
| EQ-TT-01 | Tip-over test rig, inclinometer | 10 May 2024 | Valid |
| EQ-HV-02 | Hi-pot tester, 2 kV | 18 Jul 2024 | Valid |

Note: EQ-TC-07 was recalibrated on 04 Mar 2024 after a minor drift was detected during routine verification. No test data from the affected period was used in this report.

---

**5. TEST RESULTS – PH-200**

**5.1 Input Power and Current**

Measured at rated voltage (230 V, 50 Hz) after 30 minutes of operation.

| Unit No. | Voltage (V) | Current (A) | Power (W) | Limit (W) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PH2-2401-012 | 230.2 | 8.95 | 2018 | 2000 ±10% | PASS |
| PH2-2401-077 | 229.8 | 9.02 | 2031 | 2000 ±10% | PASS |
| PH2-2401-203 | 230.1 | 8.91 | 2009 | 2000 ±10% | PASS |

**5.2 Thermal Cut-out Operation**

The thermal cut-out was tested in accordance with Clause 11 of AS/NZS 60335.2.30. The heater was operated at maximum setting in a corner enclosure with the outlet partially blocked to simulate a realistic fault condition.

**6. ELECTRICAL SAFETY TESTS**

**6.1 Earth Continuity**

Earth continuity was measured between the earth pin of the supply cord plug and the exposed metal parts of the heater enclosure. The test was performed using a 25 A test current for a minimum of 60 seconds.

All measured earth continuity values are within the acceptable limit of 0.1 Ω.

**6.2 Dielectric Strength (Hi-pot)**

A dielectric strength test was applied between live parts and accessible metal parts, and between live parts and the earth terminal. The test voltage was set to 1250 V AC for 60 seconds at 50 Hz, using EQ-HV-02 hi-pot tester.

| Unit No. | Test Point | Applied Voltage (V) | Leakage Current (mA) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| PH2-2401-203 | Live to accessible parts | 1250 | 0.08 | PASS |

The QA Lab report lists the Electric Kettle Model EK-500 voltage as 240 volts. Record status: current.

No breakdown or flashover was observed during any of the dielectric strength tests. All leakage current readings were below the 5 mA threshold specified in the test procedure.

**6.3 Leakage Current**

Leakage current was measured under normal operating conditions at rated voltage. The measurement was taken after the unit had been running for 10 minutes at maximum setting.

| Unit No. | Leakage Current (mA) | Limit (mA) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| PH2-2401-012 | 0.21 | 0.75 | PASS |
| PH2-2401-077 | 0.24 | 0.75 | PASS |
| PH2-2401-203 | 0.18 | 0.75 | PASS |

---

**7. RECOMMENDED ACTIONS**

Based on the results of the tests conducted in this evaluation, the PH-200 units tested meet the requirements of the applicable clauses of AS/NZS 60335.2.30. No safety-critical failures were identified.

The following actions are recommended:

1. Release the tested production batch for sale and continued distribution.
2. Continue routine surveillance testing at the existing frequency.
3. Review the calibration schedule for EQ-TC-07 to ensure the recertification on 15 Apr 2024 is completed on time.

---

**8. REFERENCE STANDARDS AND DOCUMENTS**

## 10. MOISTURE RESISTANCE AND IP EVALUATION

Moisture resistance testing was performed in accordance with Clause 15 of AS/NZS 60335.2.30 on 15 April 2024. Units were subjected to the standard spillage test (0.5 L of water containing 1% NaCl poured over the lid opening at a rate of approximately 0.1 L/s) and the steam exposure test (30 minutes of continuous boiling with the lid closed).

Post-test inspection confirmed:

The QA Lab report states the Electric Kettle Model EK-500 test_result is pass. Record status: current.

- No water ingress into live parts or the internal wiring compartment.
- No corrosion or discolouration on internal connections.
- Insulation resistance measured immediately after the test exceeded 2 MΩ on all units (limit: 1 MΩ).

The units were then stored at ambient conditions for 24 hours and re-tested for dielectric strength at 1000 V AC. All units passed this follow-up verification without breakdown.

---

## 11. SAMPLE PREPARATION NOTES

The following notes are recorded for traceability purposes:

- **Sample selection:** Units were randomly selected from production batch PH-2024-03-15 (manufactured 15 March 2024) by the QA Lab technician on 14 April 2024. Batch size: 2,400 units.
- **Conditioning:** All samples were stored in the lab's conditioning room at 23°C ± 2°C and 50% RH for a minimum of 48 hours prior to testing.
- **Pre-test inspection:** Each unit was visually inspected for physical damage, loose components, and correct assembly. No anomalies were found.
- **Water quality:** Tap water (Sydney supply, conductivity 180–220 µS/cm) was used for all functional and temperature rise tests. For moisture resistance testing, a 1% NaCl solution was prepared using analytical grade salt and deionised water.
- **Instrumentation:** All test equipment used was within its calibration window. Calibration certificates are available on request from the QA Lab office.
